requirement:
Every {term}`requirements.references.test_source_item` MUST carry one or more
`{test}` annotations in comments belonging to that item under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.references.coverage.tests` says: "Every test source item MUST carry one or more `{test}` annotations in comments belonging to that item under `requirements.references.outline_comments`." This is a coverage rule about which references the analysed sources must have, and about how comment placement decides which item a reference belongs to. It doesn't prescribe any library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface.

I tested each clause by asking whether a different implementation could keep the observable behavior and still break the clause:
- "Every test source item MUST carry one or more `{test}` annotations" is satisfied by the observable outcome that a test item has a `{test}` reference. How a checker finds test items or counts references is discretionary. The text imposes no structure there.
- "in comments belonging to that item under `requirements.references.outline_comments`" delegates to a cited requirement. That requirement's comment-run and ownership rules are stated as behavior: which outline node a comment run belongs to, and which line and column are retained. Cited declarations only supply context. Any outline or comment-attachment design that gives the same ownership results conforms.
- `requirements.references.test_source_item` defines what counts as a test (for Rust, a function with `#[test]` or an attribute whose path ends in `test`). It is a recognition criterion, not a structural prescription.

Every clause is therefore observable behavior. No implementation root is needed, and the review roots are empty. `requirements.references.coverage.tests` has no `Implements` edges, which is consistent with that. Whether the tests adequately verify the behavior belongs to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The requirement has one behavioral obligation. Every Rust test source item must have at least one `{test}` annotation in a comment that belongs to it under `requirements.references.outline_comments`. A test source item is a function with `#[test]` or an attribute whose path ends in `test`. This includes functions in Cargo integration-test targets.

I did not request implementation source. The reviewed tests cover the obligation as follows.

- **Annotated and unannotated cases** (`src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[test_functions_need_a_test_reference]`). It calls `untested_tests` on a mixed source and asserts the exact list of flagged names and their order.
  - Items that pass: a comment before the attribute, a comment inside the body, and a closed fenced `{test}` block.
  - A fenced `{test}` naming an unknown target still counts as a test annotation.
  - Items that are flagged: an unclosed fence, a bare `#[test]`, `#[tokio::test]` with only `{cite}`, an async `#[tokio::test(flavor=...)]`, a test in a nested `mod tests` and in an inline module, and a test with only `{impl}`.
  - Items that are not flagged: `#[cfg(test)]`, `#[rstest]`, a plain helper, and `#[doc = "... #[test] ..."]`.
  - An annotation does not leak onto the next function. The bare `untested` follows the annotated `unknown_fenced_target` and is still flagged.
  - A multiline signature with a non-ASCII name reports the right line and name.
- **Attribute path forms** (`tests/coverage.rs#fn[test_annotations_follow_the_attribute_path_and_the_comment_owner]`). It runs through `validate_repository`.
  - `#[::essais::r#test]` and `#[équipe /* … */ :: test(options)]` are flagged with the exact message and line.
  - `#[::essais::test]` with a preceding `{test}` comment passes.
  - `#[cfg_attr(test, ignore)]` is not a test.
- **Integration-test targets** (`src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[test_reference_errors_ignore_unannotated_helpers]`). A bare `#[test]` in `tests/foo.rs` yields exactly one error, at the right location, and the unannotated helper is not reported.
- **Validation errors** (`tests/coverage.rs#fn[unmarked_tests_and_parse_failures_remain_validation_errors]`). A bare test in a module is reported as an error and the helper is not.
- **Annotation counts despite target findings** (`tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_test_annotation_counts_even_when_its_target_has_a_finding]`). A `{test}` that points at a target with its own finding, or at a missing target, still satisfies this requirement. No `has no {test}` error is produced.
- **No false positives** (`tests/coverage.rs#fn[ordinary_functions_types_and_test_helpers_require_no_book_connection]`). Ordinary functions, types and helpers, plus an annotated test, produce no coverage or `no {test}` errors, either in validation or in status output.

The assertions are exact and they enforce both the positive and negative directions of the requirement. I found no unexercised obligation, so I report no gap.

text: :::{req} coverage.tests
Every {term}`requirements.references.test_source_item` MUST carry one or more
`{test}` annotations in comments belonging to that item under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{definition} source_item
:phrase: source item
A node in a project file’s outline, identified by the project-relative path
and an outline selector. For example, `src/auth.rs#fn[check_token]` identifies
a Rust function. The root node represents the whole file. A reference in a
comment belongs to the item that owns the comment under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
:::{definition} test_source_item
:phrase: test source item
A {term}`requirements.references.source_item` recognized as a test by Habeas.
In first-party Rust sources under {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`,
this is a function with `#[test]` or an attribute whose path ends in `test`,
such as `#[tokio::test]`. This includes functions in Cargo integration-test targets.
